replies.text: {"verdicts":[{"id":"T1","keep":true,"reason":"Shared-device session inheritance is a concrete spoofing attack supported by the shared-device quote."},{"id":"T2","keep":true,"reason":"Distinct repudiation harm: offline note authorship cannot be attributed; needs its own fix."},{"id":"T3","keep":true,"reason":"Design states unencrypted local SQLite cache on shared tablets; concrete disclosure attack."},{"id":"T4","keep":false,"reason":"Same attacker reading cached patient data from shared tablet cache for same harm as T3.","duplicateOf":"T3"},{"id":"T5","keep":true,"reason":"Client-side tampering of local rows/sync payloads corrupting backend records is a distinct attack."},{"id":"T6","keep":true,"reason":"Stale offline device overwriting newer clinical notes on sync; design states offline work and shared devices."},{"id":"T7","keep":true,"reason":"Revoked account retaining offline access to cached records is a distinct authorization-persistence attack."}]}
